changelog: When to Segment: merged candidate rules into concrete surface-form signals and added guidance to treat openings of subordinate clauses, temporal adjuncts, scope-limiters, appositives and naming phrases as signs to wait for their heads or complements.

Priority Rules: added a single, general demotion principle to place low confidence on any candidate that would finalise a predicate, head noun, polarity or modifier scope before disambiguating material (verbs, head nouns, coordinated items, negation complements, appositives) arrives; listed common surface tokens that typically trigger this demotion.

Decision Procedure: kept the two-step mark-then-rank flow but required that marking include extra low-ranked candidates when a sentence contains more than one parenthetical/appositive or multiple locative phrases so that the format constraint (>=4 tags in such cases) can be satisfied by the deterministic stage.
